t.5.29.1: Having thus reflected on many kinds of thoughts, the great monkey uttered sweet words within the hearing of Vaidehī.
t.5.29.2: There was a king named Daśaratha, lord of chariots, elephants and horses, virtuous in conduct, of great fame, upright and greatly renowned, born in a line of universal emperors and equal to Puraṃdara in strength.
t.5.29.3: He delights in non-violence, is free from meanness, compassionate, and of true valour; foremost of the Ikṣvāku line, he is endowed with splendour and increases the splendour of others.
t.5.29.5: His beloved eldest son, whose face resembles the lord of the stars, is named Rāma; he is a man of discerning knowledge and the foremost of all who bear the bow.
t.5.29.4: Endowed with the marks of royalty, of abundant splendour, a bull among kings, he was renowned throughout the four-bounded earth, a giver of happiness and himself happy.
t.5.29.6: He is the protector of his own conduct and the protector of his own people as well; that scorcher of foes is the protector of the world of living beings and of dharma.
t.5.29.7: At the word of his aged father, who was true to his promise, the hero went forth into the forest with his wife and together with his brother.
t.5.29.8: While he was roaming there in the great forest, chasing game, Rāvaṇa heard of the slaughter at Janasthāna and that Khara and Dūṣaṇa had been slain. Then, out of resentment, Jānakī was carried off by Rāvaṇa.
t.5.29.10: Having spoken these words thus, that bull among monkeys fell silent; and Jānakī too, hearing that, was filled with the greatest wonder.
t.5.29.9: She whose form, whose complexion and whose beauty I heard set forth with certainty by Rāghava, this is that very lady, now found by me.
t.5.29.11: Then she, the timid one with lovely hair whose locks curled at their tips, raised her face, veiled by her hair, and gazed at the śiṃśapā tree.
t.5.29.12: Looking sideways, upward and also downward, she saw him of inconceivable intelligence, the minister of the lord of the tawny ones, the son of the Wind, like the sun standing at its rising.
